content.comment_body: I am working on a two-way valve to control heating for two water tanks. Tank 1 should always maintain 53 degrees. For Tank 2, if its temperature drops below 30 degrees, relay Q3 should be activated. If Tank 1 falls below 53 degrees, Q3 should deactivate, and when Tank 1 returns to 53 degrees, Q3 should reactivate until Tank 2 reaches 30 degrees. Of course, when Tank 2 reaches 30 degrees, Q3 should deactivate. I’ve got most of it working, but not quite as desired. Currently, when Tank 1 drops by 4 degrees, Q3 deactivates, but activating Q3 again happens too quickly when Tank 1 increases by just 1 degree. Please review the attachment for details.
I’ve shared an attachment with a potential solution for the issue.
Thank you, this seems to work just as I wanted.

Thank you very much, [user_name]. I have another problem now. In the same program, I want to add additional functions. If Tank 1 keeps dropping more than 4 degrees, I want to activate a second relay. Up to a maximum of 53 degrees for Tank 1, for example, if it drops 7 degrees, the second relay should activate—and I’d like this threshold to be adjustable. Do I need another PT100 sensor or is it possible to integrate this with the first function? Any guidance would be appreciated as I’m trying to learn more about this.
No need for an extra PT100 sensor. You can configure multiple switching thresholds using the same measured temperature, by programming parallel threshold triggers.
You’ve helped me a lot—thank you so much, [user_name]. I understand temperature control much better now, thanks to your example. I hope I can reach out again if I encounter another issue.

Hello again, [user_name]. I’ve loaded the program into [product_name] [version_no]—it works fine. But the web server isn’t accessible in my browser, even though I have enabled it. I think I might need to add a runtime counter to get the web server working, but I’m not sure how to incorporate this. Please help.
Why did you ask the question twice? [url]

Do you know how the web server works with [product_name]? How do you enable and access it on [product_name] [version_no]? For every message you want displayed on the web server, you have to activate the message text in the settings. This isn’t enabled in my program because you hadn’t mentioned using the web server previously.

Hello [user_name]! Thanks for your quick reply. I’m not sure why I asked twice—I saw my first question didn’t appear in our conversation, so I tried again. Yes, I do know about the web server and I followed the necessary steps, as you described. Still, it’s not working for me—the browser can’t display the page.
It’s working now—I realized I needed to set it to run mode. Sorry for missing that step.
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread, regarding adding a Summer/Winter switch to enable or disable Q3 depending on the season. Best regards, [user_name]
